title: Lufthansa 502
summary: Flight 502 crashed on approach to Rio de Janeiro after descending below the minimum cleared altitude during rainy weather. The aircraft struck the water with its nosewheel and the crew was unable to maintain control. Investigation found pilot error in descending below the cleared altitude, with crew fatigue from exceeding maximum permitted flight times according to Brazilian regulations contributing to the accident.
probable_cause: Pilot error resulting in descending below the altitude cleared for the approach. Crew fatigue from exceeding maximum permitted flight times according to Brazilian aviation regulations was a contributing factor.

factors.evidence: The crew had exceeded the maximum permitted flight times according to Brazilian aviation regulations.

Descending too low on approach, the Constellation struck the water with the aircraft's nosewheel.
The aircraft crashed near Flecheiras Beach just short of the runway.

During the descent in rainy weather, the aircraft descended too low on approach.

title: American Airlines 320
summary: American Airlines Flight 320, a Lockheed L-188 Electra flying from Chicago to New York, crashed into the East River about 4,900 ft short of runway 22 while approaching LaGuardia Airport through a 400 ft overcast ceiling and fog, killing 65 of 73 aboard. The Civil Aeronautics Board found the crew, new to the Electra, flew below the intended approach path while the altimeter appeared to show a safe altitude; the Air Line Pilots Association instead blamed faulty instruments. It was the first crash involving the Electra type.
probable_cause: The Civil Aeronautics Board concluded the crew made mistakes that caused the crash, with the crew's inexperience on the Electra and poor weather conditions cited as contributing factors.

events.text: The LaGuardia approach controller advised the pilots of an overcast ceiling of 400 ft and visibility of 1.25 mi, and instructed them to prepare for approach to runway 22 over the East River.
Surviving flight crew members said that, right up to the moment of impact, the altimeter had been showing they were flying a safe distance above the water.
LaGuardia tower gave the flight its final landing clearance for runway 22 when it was 2.8 mi from the airport; the crew acknowledged only with '320' and there were no further radio communications.
A witness in a car near the Whitestone Bridge saw the aircraft pass overhead only about 100 ft above the ground, lower than planes usually flew in the area.
Flying at 140 knots, the aircraft struck the East River about 4900 ft short of the runway.

notes: CAB blamed crew error/inexperience; ALPA disputed and blamed faulty instruments -- both perspectives noted

title: TWA 891
summary: A Lockheed L-1649A Starliner carrying 59 passengers and 9 crew departed Milan Malpensa for Paris on June 26, 1959 in light rain and thunderstorms. Twelve minutes after takeoff while climbing through 10,000 feet, the aircraft suffered structural failure and broke up in mid-air. An Italian inquiry determined that a lightning strike ignited flammable vapors in fuel tank number 7, causing explosions that destroyed the aircraft structure.
probable_cause: Lightning ignited gasoline vapors in the fuel tanks through static electricity discharge, causing explosions that destroyed the aircraft's structural integrity during flight.

factors.evidence: Thunderstorms were in the area at the time of departure with light rain and low overcast.
The breaking-up in flight was due to the explosion of the fuel vapors contained in tank number 7, followed immediately by either an explosion of pressure or a further explosion in tank #6.
The Starliner suffered structural failure and broke up in mid-air.

events.text: Departed Milan Malpensa Airport with light rain, low overcast ceiling of approximately 2,000 feet, visibility of two miles and thunderstorms in the area.

title: TAI 307
summary: The DC-7C departed Bordeaux at night with light drizzle and limited visibility. Following takeoff, the aircraft reached only 30 m altitude and failed to climb further before flying into a pine forest 2950 m from the runway. The aircraft cut a swath through the forest, and the fuselage broke up before post-crash fire destroyed the wreckage.
probable_cause: With lack of visual references in darkness, the pilot failed to maintain optimum climbing speed and did not carefully monitor the altimeter, allowing the aircraft to descend back to terrain level.

A pilot may follow a line of flight that will bring the aircraft back near the ground if the altimeter is not carefully watched.
The aircraft flew into a pine forest located 2950 m from the end of the runway after reaching only 30 m altitude.

title: Braniff 542
summary: Braniff Flight 542 broke apart in mid-air without warning while cruising at 15,000 feet east of Waco, Texas. Witnesses reported seeing a blinding flash and explosion with flaming objects falling for several seconds. The left wing separated from the fuselage and landed over a mile from the main crash site. The aircraft was only nine days in service. The investigation identified structural integrity issues with the Electra after similar crashes of other aircraft.

title: Piedmont Airlines 349
summary: Flight 349, a Douglas DC-3, was on an ILS approach to Charlottesville when the aircraft descended below safe altitude during an inbound turn. The wing clipped the ground and the aircraft struck Bucks Elbow Mountain at 2600 feet. Investigation determined a lateral course error from navigational omission was not corrected, with mental stress on the captain as a contributing factor.
probable_cause: Navigational omission resulting in a lateral course error not detected and corrected through precision instrument flying procedures. Contributing factor was pre-occupation of the captain from mental stress.

title: National Airlines 967
summary: National Airlines Flight 967, a Douglas DC-7B, disappeared over the Gulf of Mexico en route from Tampa to New Orleans. At 12:44 AM, the captain reported a smooth flight with unlimited visibility but noted a solid overcast of fog ahead. The aircraft was cleared to descend to 5,000 feet, but the control tower reported actual ceiling of 1,200 feet with visibility of three-fourths mile in light fog and rain. Radar picked up the flight at 12:46 AM and observed it turn toward New Orleans, then the aircraft disappeared from radar at 12:51 AM and never responded to subsequent radio calls. All 42 aboard were presumed killed.

title: Aeroflot 315 (1959)
summary: Aeroflot Flight 315 crashed short of Lviv Airport runway during final approach in icing conditions. The aircraft descended normally in cold weather with humidity 97%, switched to visual flight rules after descending through clouds, and at 110 meters altitude the flaps were set to 45 degrees. The aircraft then experienced a rapid pitch down and crashed 2100 meters from the runway in a 25-degree nose-down attitude.
probable_cause: Anomaly in the engine power control system combined with substandard placement of cockpit controls; pitot tube icing caused erroneous airspeed readings; icing of the horizontal stabilizer created a supercritical angle of attack when flaps lowered to 45 degrees.

events.text: Flight 315 departed Vnukovo Airport at 16:48 Moscow time and was cleared to climb to 7000 meters.
As the airliner approached Lviv, the weather was reported as temperature -1 degree C, humidity 97% with the possibility of icing conditions.
Before reaching the inner marker, the aircraft descended out of the clouds and the crew switched to visual flight rules.
At 19:06 while descending through 110 meters, the flaps were set to 45 degrees.
The Antonov began a rapid pitch down 2100 meters from the runway in a 25 degree nose down attitude.
The aircraft crashed, flipped over and burst into flames with the impact and post-crash fire killing all on board.

notes: Investigation detailed with subsequent An-10 crash three months later confirming stabilizer icing issue

title: Ariana Afghan Airlines 202
summary: A Douglas DC-4 with registration YA-BAG departed Beirut at 1:30 AM Local Time and crashed into the side of a hill in Aramoun two minutes after takeoff, killing 24 of 27 occupants. The investigation found the pilot did not properly execute a right turn, possibly due to distraction or forgetfulness, and the aircraft was experiencing fire in the No. 1 engine which induced emergency actions reducing turn and climb performance.
probable_cause: The pilot did not properly execute a right turn as early as he should have, either because he forgot or was distracted by some unusual occurrence, and a fire in the No. 1 engine induced the pilot to start emergency actions with a resulting reduction in the rate of turn and climb.
